analysis.title: Weekly HF Highlights: HFs Turn Sellers of AI Infrastructure; Limited Appetite to Add Risk Globally
key_insights: HFs ended the week (through Thursday Oct 8) as larger net sellers of global equities as concerns about the AI Infrastructure complex accelerated, alongside a continued focus on rates.
North America selling was the largest since July, mostly from the long side, with shorts more muted, implying HFs reduced both net and gross exposure.
Selling was concentrated in a narrow group of themes, with TMT and Health Care accounting for the largest share of activity.
In TMT, HFs sold longs and added shorts amid debates over the physical constraints of the AI Infrastructure complex. Semis (Analog and Semi Caps) and Optical Networking were the most net sold.
Agentic AI Beneficiaries (MSXXCLAW Index constituents) were net sold this week after being net bought for much of September.
In Health Care, selling came mostly from Biotech (more Large Cap and Commercial than Pre-Commercial) and AI Health Care names, almost entirely from the long side.
Defensives were preferred over Cyclicals. Staples, Utilities and Real Estate were net bought. Discretionary, Industrials, Materials and Energy were net sold.
The defensive bid is consistent with HFs running lighter gross, a higher quality bias and a large-cap over small-cap bias.
HFs sold every non-US region. Japan saw the largest supply, followed by AxJ, then Europe.
In Japan, HFs sold all single-name sectors except Health Care. Selling skewed to SMID-caps, leaving HFs net buyers of the Size factor.

In AxJ, most supply came from China, where A and H-shares were sold in similar size. China Industrials, TMT and Health Care drove it. HFs were also net sellers of Memory in broader Asia, led by Korea.
European equities were net sold in small amounts, but HFs sold high-conviction longs in relatively large size, based on flows to the Top 50 Crowded EU Longs.
Q4 has started poorly for HFs, with alpha under pressure on both long and short sides. Crowded TMT and Health Care positions drove the weaker Americas L/S performance.
Return dispersion is very wide. The 25th percentile Global L/S fund is down about 2% YTD, the 75th percentile is up 13%, and roughly 30% of L/S funds are negative YTD.
On Oct 8 the Top 50 Crowded Longs lost 1.87% against a 0.29% drop for the Top 50 Shorts, a daily spread of -1.57%.

sector_views.rationale: HF flows were net buying in all three during the week to Oct 8, consistent with reluctance to add risk.
HFs sold longs and added shorts in AI Infrastructure themes, with Semis and Optical Networking the most net sold.
Large Cap and Commercial Biotech and AI Health Care were net sold, almost entirely from the long side.
All four were net sold by HFs this week.

risk_factors: Physical constraints of the AI Infrastructure complex are driving debate and HF de-risking.
Rates remain a continued focus for HF positioning.
Crowded TMT and Health Care positions are hurting HF alpha in Q4.
Selling of high-conviction EU longs signals a pivot away from crowded positions.
vol_and_positioning: US L/S net leverage was flat WoW at 52% (52nd percentile since 2010). Gross leverage rose 1% WoW to 207% (91st percentile since 2010).
Europe gross leverage is 171% (21st percentile since 2010) and net leverage is 54% (92nd percentile since 2010). Asia gross is 126% (18th percentile) and net is 62% (65th percentile).
Top 50 Crowding Performance (Longs minus Shorts): WTD -0.8%, MTD -0.5%, YTD +23.9%.
N. America Top 50 Crowded Longs: WTD -0.76%, MTD +0.95%, YTD +38.76%, against the S&P 500 at +14.43% YTD.
Europe Top 50 Crowded Longs: WTD -3.13%, MTD -4.26%, YTD -1.05%, a -2.73% weekly spread to the Top 50 Shorts.
Asia Top 50 Crowded Longs: WTD -1.30%, MTD +0.50%, YTD +35.53%.
HFs are running lighter gross exposure with a higher quality bias and a large-cap over small-cap bias.
